title: Контроль на каждом шагу  (Control at Every Step)

segments.t: At Arcobaleno, Viktor snaps at Elena for watching his every move in the kitchen, while back at Claude Monet German catches sous-chef Lyova helping Denis and orders him onto potato duty. Listen in Russian first.
Пойди в салон красоты, что-нибудь сделай.
С этого момента отправляйтесь на заготовки.
Let's look closely at each Russian line in this scene.
'Did you not forget the salt?' Elena keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'I did not forget anything at all.' In spoken Russian, Chef Viktor omits unnecessary linking verbs so the key idea lands immediately.
'Why are you controlling everything in here?' Chef Viktor keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'You have been following me around all day.' In spoken Russian, Chef Viktor omits unnecessary linking verbs so the key idea lands immediately.
'Do you have nothing else to do?' Chef Viktor addresses the listener with the informal singular pronoun, showing a close or familiar relationship.
Пойди в салон красоты, что-нибудь сделай.
'Go to a beauty salon, do something for yourself.' Chef Viktor uses natural conversational word order here to highlight the most important part of the reply.
'Sorry, I got carried away...' Chef Viktor keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'Would you care for a massage as well?' German keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
С этого момента отправляйтесь на заготовки.
'From this moment on, report to vegetable prep.' German uses natural conversational word order here to highlight the most important part of the reply.
'Go peel potatoes.' German keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'Alright, Viktor Petrovich.' In spoken Russian, Elena omits unnecessary linking verbs so the key idea lands immediately.
'Get to work.' German uses natural conversational word order here to highlight the most important part of the reply. With all the phrases clear, listen to the full Russian dialogue again.
Пойди в салон красоты, что-нибудь сделай.
С этого момента отправляйтесь на заготовки.
That covers Viktor snapping at Elena for hovering over him and advising her to visit a beauty salon. Notice how Russian reflexive verbs express finding something to do. See you in the next scene.
